catalog_quote: 2.1.2. Словесное ударение в У.я. динамическое, падает, за исключением поздних русских заимствований, сохраняющих ударение оригинала, и некоторых глагольных, местоименных и наречных форм, на последний слог слова.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-strict, final syllable' (final stress) is exactly what both held sources say: Kel'makov 1993:241 ('падает.. на последний слог слова') and Borise & Georgieva 2024:318,320 (final stress in all word classes, shifting to the rightmost inflectional suffix), with the 2024 acoustic results (§6, p.352) showing duration, intensity, f0 and F1 all cue the stressed final syllable. Both quotations were verified verbatim at the stated pages in the text files we hold. The record's 'grade' field is blank even though it rests on a specialist sketch plus a current JIPA instrumental study, so the only action is to record an strength of the evidence (top tier). sources.note: Stress-only article (keywords 'prosody, word stress'): Udmurt has fixed word-final stress; lists the Lower Cheptsa deviations (penult stress in verb forms with -my/-dy/-zy, initial or vacillating stress in reduplicated/intensive adjectives, -ak adverbs, interrogative-pronoun forms etc.) with North Udmurt parallels. a full-text search for stress/accent the full text: no mention of tone, pitch or melody.

tone.quote: В удмуртском языке слоговое ударение – силовое, оно, как правило, падает на последний слог слова [5. С. 79; 7. С. 172]. Слово (слог), которому придается особенно важное значение в предложении, произносится с усилением голоса и с резким повышением тона на его ударном слоге [5. С. 76, 77]
tone.translation: In Udmurt, syllable (word) stress is dynamic; as a rule it falls on the last syllable of the word. The word (syllable) that is given particular importance in the sentence is pronounced with intensified voice and a sharp rise in pitch on its stressed syllable.
